text:
alex: Heads-up — we're finalizing the SLO-driven routing behavior for priority tiers and I want to lock down how fallbacks + quotas interact. Quick brain dump and questions below.

maria: Nice. Do you mean the flow where a Platinum request can fall back to a quantized variant or to Gold capacity if latency SLO is at risk?

alex: Exactly. Proposed rules: if p95 latency > tier_SLO for 30s, start routing new requests to fallback_model_variant (same accuracy class but lower cost) until p95 recovers. If errors spike (5%+ over 1m) trigger circuit-breaker and route to next compatible region or capacity tier. Thoughts? :thinking_face:

kevin: Quick clarification — are we distinguishing "fallback to model variant" versus "fallback to capacity tier/region"? They have different billing and quota semantics.

alex: Yes. Two orthogonal actions: 1) model-variant fallback (cheap/fast) within same capacity, 2) routing fallback across region/tier (affects quotas/reserved capacity).

product-liz: From UX perspective console should show active fallback policy and allow manual override per-customer. Also surface reason: latency vs error_cb. We need clear labels like "SLO-triggered model fallback" vs "CB-triggered cross-region failover".

jordan: For circuit-breaker thresholds, can we use: error_rate >= 5% sustained for 60s OR consecutive_5xx >= 10 in 30s to trip? And auto-reset after 5m if healthy?

rami: Those numbers look sensible as starting defaults. My only ask: make them configurable per-customer and per-route. Enterprise customers will want stricter thresholds.

kevin: Also watch out for double-fallback loops: if model fallback increases latency slightly or changes traffic patterns it could cascade across regions. We should enforce a cooldown and a rollout window e.g., apply variant fallback only to 10% traffic for first 60s then ramp to 100% if metrics improve.

alex: Good point. Proposal: staged rollout (10/50/100) over configurable windows. And add a global rate limiter so fallback ramps don't exceed capacity quotas.

maria: Telemetry needs: metric tags for triggering_reason (latency|error|quota) + before_variant + after_variant + rollout_percent + customer_tier. Dashboards should show triggered events as spikes on the tier's SLO charts.

product-liz: UX: add a toast/annotation in route history when a fallback is active with a one-click rollback. Also expose simulation mode in console: "preview fallback traffic" that simulates routing without billing changes.

jordan: Internal API debate: Should routing decision be centralized in control-plane or pushed down to local edge proxies? Centralized gives coherent decisions but adds latency; edge local gives speed but inconsistent global view.

rami: I'd prefer hybrid: central policy engine emits rules and thresholds; edge proxies evaluate metrics locally and call central service when ambiguous. That reduces control-plane QPS while keeping consistent configs.

kevin: We need a compact operator API for these policies. Sketch:
```json
{
  "policy_id": "p-123",
  "priority_tier": "platinum",
  "slo_p95_ms": 100,
  "fallbacks": [
    {"type": "model_variant", "variant_id": "v-quant-8bit", "stages": [10,50,100], "cooldown_s": 60},
    {"type": "region_failover", "regions": ["us-west-2","eu-central-1"], "quota_aware": true}
  ],
  "circuit_breaker": {"error_rate_pct": 5, "window_s": 60, "consecutive_5xx": 10, "auto_reset_s": 300}
}
```

alex: That looks great — just ensure we include "apply_to_routes": [] and an optional "simulate": true flag.

maria: One more: quotas. If a Platinum customer has reserved Dedicated capacity, we should prefer that capacity for fallbacks and avoid routing them to shared-hosted unless reserved is exhausted. Console should surface reserved vs shared usage bars.

product-liz: Agreed. Also add billing visibility for fallbacks (estimated delta cost) so customers understand cost impact of an emergency failover.

jordan: Ops question: who gets paged when a fallback triggers? Oncall for the affected stack (runtime) + account owner if enterprise tier. We should create a specific alert type: "fallback_triggered" with context.

rami: Implementation tasks I see: policy model + validation, control-plane API, edge evaluation logic, rollout controller, telemetry hooks + dashboards, console UI changes, billing delta calc. I'll split into tickets.

deploy-bot: deploy:policy-service v2.14 started at 1771002900 — running smoke checks. :rocket:

alex: Thanks everyone — I'll consolidate defaults and open a PR with the policy schema and console mocks. Posting draft RFC later today.

maria: Awesome, ping me on the RFC for telemetry spec.

kevin: Ping me for the edge proxy changes.

product-liz: I'll work on the UI copy and mockups.

alex: Closing thread for now — if anyone has follow-ups add them here, otherwise RFC coming. :+1:
